rounds.proof_sketch: Original clamps predictions min to 1e-12; mutant clamps to 0. When input has exact 0s, original produces tiny positive values after normalization while mutant produces exact 0s. CUDA kernel skips terms where p=0, causing ~13.5 difference per batch vs tolerance of 0.01.
rounds.survival_reason: Standard random inputs (torch.rand) produce values in [0,1) that are almost always >> 1e-12, so neither clamping threshold affects them. The Layer 2 testing with random seeds didn't find divergence because it didn't test explicit zeros. The mutation only manifests with carefully crafted inputs containing exact zeros or values in (0, 1e-12).
rounds.kill_strategy: Create predictions tensor with explicit zeros (half zeros, half ones) so that after clamping and normalization, mutant produces p=0 values that cause kernel to skip those KL terms entirely, while original produces tiny positive p values that contribute large terms due to very negative log(p).
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for numerical stability guards should include edge-case inputs with exact boundary values (zeros, near-epsilon values) rather than relying solely on random sampling which rarely hits these boundary conditions.
rounds.suggested_code:
def generate_inputs(device):
    # Predictions: alternating 1s and 0s
    predictions = torch.zeros(128, 4096, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    predictions[:, ::2] = 1.0  # Even indices = 1.0, odd indices = 0.0
    
    # Targets: uniform positive values
    targets = torch.ones(128, 4096, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    
    return [predictions, targets]
